discovery: Coherent control and optical readout of individual electron and nuclear spins in solid-state defects (nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond), establishing solid-state spin qubits for quantum sensing and quantum networks
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state quantum optics and quantum information
motivation: Wrachtrup pioneered optical detection and coherent manipulation of single spins in diamond, demonstrating that an individual defect in a solid can be initialised, controlled and read out at room temperature. Awschalom established coherent control of single spins in semiconductors and diamond, including ultrafast manipulation and coupling to spin environments, turning defect spins into an engineered quantum platform. Lukin showed how nearby nuclear spins serve as long-lived quantum memories and introduced nanoscale magnetometry with single NV centres, while developing spin-photon interfaces for quantum repeaters. Together, their discoveries created a new field: individual atom-like spins in solids as qubits. This platform now enables nanoscale magnetic resonance of single molecules and cells, sensing of condensed-matter phenomena, the first loophole-free Bell test, and multi-node quantum networks. It is a rare case where fundamental single-quantum-system physics became a broadly used tool across physics, chemistry and biology.
